message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States, ranked by passenger traffic and importance:

| Airport | City / State | IATA Code | Notable Features |
|---------|--------------|-----------|------------------|
| Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) | Atlanta, GA | ATL | Largest airport in the world by passenger traffic; major hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) | Los Angeles, CA | LAX | Major gateway to Asia and Latin America; hub for American Airlines and Delta. |
| Chicago O’Hare International Airport (ORD) | Chicago, IL | ORD | One of the busiest airports in the U.S.; hub for United Airlines and American. |
| Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) | Dallas–Fort Worth, TX | DFW | Hub for American Airlines; one of the largest single-runway airports. |
| Denver International Airport (DEN) | Denver, CO | DEN | Largest airport in the U.S. by land area; hub for United and Southwest. |
| John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) | New York City, NY | JFK | Major international gateway; hub for JetBlue, Delta, and American. |
| San Francisco International Airport (SFO) | San Francisco, CA | SFO | Hub for United and a key gateway to Asia. |
| Seattle–Tacoma International Airport (SEA) | Seattle, WA | SEA | Hub for Alaska Airlines and a growing hub for Delta. |
| Miami International Airport (MIA) | Miami, FL | MIA | Major hub for LATAM and a key gateway to Latin America. |
| Orlando International Airport (MCO) | Orlando, FL | MCO | Hub for Southwest; major destination for tourism. |

These airports serve as major hubs for domestic and international flights and handle millions of passengers each year.
